# The Lights That Wait for Morning

## Scripture

*"But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession, that you may declare the praises of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light."* — 1 Peter 2:9 (NIV)

## Reflection

Before dawn, the sky holds its breath. Venus may still glimmer low on the horizon, and a few bright stars linger—but they are already fading, outshone by the approaching sunrise. They don't fight the light. They simply yield to it.

This is the quiet drama of every morning sky: darkness doesn't surrender all at once. It retreats slowly, star by star, until the whole sky is flooded with gold. Peter uses this same image for our lives. We were called *out of darkness into his wonderful light*—not by our own brightness, but by the One who rose upon us.

Perhaps you feel like a fading star this season, small against a vast sky, unsure if your light matters. Remember: even the faintest morning star declares the coming of the day. Your witness—your kindness, your faithfulness, your quiet hope—points toward a Light greater than yourself. You are God's special possession, chosen to reflect His glory.

And the best part? The sunrise is not the end of the stars. It is the promise that night will not last forever.

## Prayer

Lord of light and morning, thank You for calling us out of darkness. When we feel small or dim, remind us that we reflect Your brightness, not our own. Let our lives point others toward the coming Day. In Jesus' name, amen.
